transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. I, uh, I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time with this. 

Honestly, I'm doing okay for the most part. I can sleep fine, and I'm keeping up with everything at work—I manage an IT department, so I stay pretty busy. But, well, mostly I came in because I’m just... tired, in a way that doesn’t really make sense to me. Even with the sleep and getting my work done, I still feel like I’m running on a low battery before the day even gets going. 

I don't want to make a big deal out of it, but is that something you see often? I just want to make sure I'm doing the right thing by coming in.
Do you find that you’re less interested in things you used to enjoy, or do you feel down or hopeless more days than not?

Well, I wouldn't exactly use the word hopeless. I have a good life, and I really don't want to sound like I'm complaining or being ungrateful. But... I guess, well, for a long time now there’s just been this sort of... gray, flat feeling most days. 

It's a bit embarrassing to admit, but even things I usually look forward to—like going fishing, or tending to my tomatoes out back, or even taking in a church concert—they just feel more like items on a checklist lately, instead of something I actually enjoy doing. I just kind of go through the motions to get them done. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it right.
Do you often feel fatigued or like you don’t have much energy to get through the day?

Well, yes, I suppose I do. And I know I mentioned this a moment ago, so I hope I'm not repeating myself too much. But that's really the main reason I decided to come in. 

I just... I feel tired, but it's a strange kind of tired. It doesn't really make sense to me, because, like I said, I'm sleeping fine and I'm getting all my work done at the office. But even so, I wake up and it just feels like my battery is already low before I've even started my day. 

I don't want to make it sound worse than it is—I'm still functioning and everything, I promise. It's just this constant, lingering lack of energy. Is that... is that helpful? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Would you say that you feel down or sad most of the day, nearly every day?

Well, I know I touched on this a little bit earlier, and I hope it's okay that I'm bringing it up again. I wouldn't call it a deep sadness, necessarily. I don't want you to think I'm sitting around crying all day or anything like that. 

But... yes, I suppose for a long time now, there has been this sort of gray, flat feeling that just hangs around most days. It's like I was saying before, about the fishing and the tomatoes and the church concerts. I used to really get a kick out of those things, but lately, they just feel like chores I have to check off a list. 

I'm really trying my best to stay positive, though. I hope I'm not coming across as too negative or difficult. Does that answer what you were asking?
Do you find it harder than usual to focus, make decisions, or think clearly during the day?

Well, no, I don't think I've had any trouble with that, thankfully. Like I mentioned, I'm still getting all my work done at the office. I manage IT systems, so I kind of have to be able to make decisions and troubleshoot all day long. And... well, my mind still feels pretty sharp. I haven't noticed any fog or anything like that. 

I hope that's okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you an accurate picture. I really don't want to make it sound like everything is falling apart for me, because it really isn't. My focus is doing just fine, I promise. Am I giving you the right kind of details?
Have you found yourself feeling more guilty or critical of yourself than usual, even about small things, or felt like you're not living up to your own standards or expectations?

Well, no, not really. I mean, I try to hold myself to a good standard, especially at work, but I don't think I'm overly hard on myself. I certainly don't sit around feeling guilty about things. 

I know I've been talking about feeling a bit flat and tired, but I really want to assure you that I'm not beating myself up or feeling worthless. I know I'm doing a good job providing for myself and keeping up with my responsibilities. I hope that's the kind of answer you're looking for? I just don't want you to worry that I'm in a really dark place or anything, because I'm honestly not. Is that... does that make sense?
How long have you been feeling this way—this flatness and low energy—with most days being affected?

Well, let's see... I guess it's been a while now. I hope it doesn't sound like I've just been ignoring it, but I'd say it's been going on since they pulled me back into full operational leadership at the company. That was... gosh, about two years and four months ago, roughly. 

It's just that taking on all those extra responsibilities again, well, it kind of took the wind out of my sails a bit. But I'm still managing, you know? I really don't want it to sound like I'm complaining or can't handle my job, because I absolutely can. It's just been a bit of a long stretch of feeling this way since that change happened. Does that timeline help give you what you need?
Have you ever had periods where your mood was unusually high, irritable, or you felt more energetic than usual, even if others around you didn’t seem to notice or thought it was out of the ordinary?

Oh, no, I've never really had anything like that. I'm a pretty even-keeled guy, honestly. I mean, sure, I have good days where I feel productive and get a lot done at the office, but it's never been anything extreme or... or out of control. I definitely don't get unusually irritable or wired. 

I try to just stay steady and reliable, you know? I hope it's alright that I don't have anything like that to report. I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you're looking for. Does that help rule things out for you?
Would you say that you no longer take pleasure or interest in activities you used to enjoy, even if you still do them?

Well, I try to stay active, I really do. I don't want to be the kind of guy who just sits around and complains. But... I suppose if I'm being completely honest—and I want to make sure I'm giving you the right information here—for a long time now, there's just been this... this sort of gray, flat feeling most days. 

It's like, even the things I always used to look forward to, you know, like going out fishing, or tending to the tomatoes in the yard, or even going to a church concert... they just feel a bit more like items on a checklist lately instead of something I actually enjoy. I still do them, of course! I make sure to get out there. It's just that the joy isn't quite the same. 

I hope it doesn't sound like I'm giving up or anything, because I'm definitely not. I'm trying my best to keep a good attitude about it all. Does that make sense? Is that the kind of detail that's helpful for you?
Have you noticed that you’ve lost interest or pleasure in most activities, even ones that aren’t part of your usual routine?

Well, I guess... I mean, I think I kind of covered that a bit just now, right? I hope I didn't confuse things. But, um, to answer your question directly... I wouldn't say I've lost interest in *most* activities. I still try to keep busy and be helpful where I can. 

Even with new things, or things outside my usual routine, I try to go into them with a good attitude. I really don't want to be a wet blanket, you know? It's just... like I said, there's that flat feeling that sort of tags along with me, no matter what I'm doing. But I still try to participate and be a good sport. I hope that's the right kind of answer? I just want to make sure I'm giving you a clear picture without sounding too negative.
Would you say that you take little or no pleasure in almost all activities, even those you used to enjoy?

I feel like I might be repeating myself a little, and I'm so sorry if I'm not giving you the exact answer you need. I really want to be helpful here. 

I definitely wouldn't say "almost all" activities, no. I mean, I still get some satisfaction out of a hard day's work, or helping a neighbor fix something, you know? I don't want you to think I'm just sitting in a dark room all day. I try very hard to keep moving and stay productive. It's just... well, like I mentioned, the *fun* part of things is just a bit dimmed down. But I still do them, and I still try to find the good in them. 

Does that... does that answer your question better? I hope I'm not making this too difficult for you to figure out.

Oh, gosh, did I... did I misunderstand the question a second ago? I'm so sorry if I'm making you repeat yourself. I really want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need for your notes. 

But, um, no, I definitely wouldn't say it's *almost all* activities. Like I was trying to say—and maybe I didn't phrase it very well—I still get a good bit of satisfaction out of things. You know, solving a tough problem at work, getting the systems running smoothly for my team, that kind of thing still feels good. I'm really not completely miserable or anything like that, I promise. I try to keep a very positive outlook and push through that flat feeling when it happens. 

I hope that makes sense? Please let me know if I'm not answering this the right way, I can try to explain it differently if you need me to.

To be completely clear... no. I don't think I've lost pleasure in almost all activities. I really do still enjoy things, especially my work and keeping busy. I'm so sorry if that's still not the answer you're looking for. Am I misunderstanding what you mean by "almost all"? I can try to rethink it if I'm doing this wrong.
